Simulate rank-ordered choice data

Source: R/simulate.R
rrologit.Rd

Draws rankings from the rank-ordered logit of rologit(): utilities from beta (and gamma) as in rmnl() plus independent standard Gumbel errors; each case ranks its alternatives by utility. depth keeps only the first positions (the rest unranked, rank 0), and ties merges each ranked position into the one above it with that probability, independently of the order within the merged group, which is the coarsening under which the exact tie likelihood of rologit() is the likelihood of the reported ranking.

Usage

rrologit(
  n,
  beta,
  gamma = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  depth = NULL,
  ties = 0
)

Arguments

n

Number of cases.

beta

A \(p \times (J-1)\) matrix: rows are the intercept and the \(p - 1\) covariates, columns the non-base alternatives (column names become their labels; the base is "a" unless levels is given).

gamma

Optional generic coefficients on alternative-specific covariates w1, w2, ... (standard normal draws for every case and alternative). The data are in the long layout with or without them (see Value).

x

Optional data frame of case-specific covariates (n rows) to use instead of standard normal draws.

levels

Optional labels of all \(J\) alternatives (base first).

depth

Optional number of ranked positions (default: every alternative is ranked).

ties

Probability that a ranked position is tied with the position above it (default 0).

Value

A data frame in the long layout, one row per case and alternative: id, alt, rank (1 = most preferred; equal values are ties; 0 = unranked), the w's and the x's, ready for rank ~ w1 | x1 + x2 with id = "id", alt = "alt". The true parameters are in the attribute "truth".

See also

rologit(), rmnl()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rrologit(300, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1), c = c(-0.3, 0.6), d = c(0.2, 0.4)), depth = 2)
head(d, 8)
#>   id alt rank         x1
#> 1  1   a    2 -0.6264538
#> 2  1   b    1 -0.6264538
#> 3  1   c    0 -0.6264538
#> 4  1   d    0 -0.6264538
#> 5  2   a    1  0.1836433
#> 6  2   b    0  0.1836433
#> 7  2   c    0  0.1836433
#> 8  2   d    2  0.1836433
